events_chronological: In a hill village in the old country, the local strongman Peppino has Emilio Nardi's father and brother killed and sends his men after the nine-year-old boy.
Emilio's mother is shot dead bargaining for his life, and the boy is smuggled overseas and renamed Emilio Rocca at the immigration station.
Grown up in the immigrant quarter, Emilio loses his grocery job when the extortionist Serafino forces the owner to hire his nephew instead.
Bruno draws Emilio into hiding a cache of guns and then into stealing a rug, beginning their partnership.
Serafino demands a cut of the young men's take, and Emilio persuades Bruno and Aldo to let him handle it his own way.
During the neighbourhood festival Emilio shoots Serafino dead on his own staircase and quietly assumes his place as the local protector.
Emilio builds an olive oil importing company and settles neighbourhood grievances, forcing an old widow's landlord to back down.
Emilio sails back to the old country and guts the aged Peppino with a knife, closing the vendetta.
The family gathers to surprise Emilio on his birthday, and his youngest son Dante announces he has enlisted in the infantry.
At the lake house decades later, Dante conducts business through his son's first communion party while his sister Rosa asks leave to marry a man named Wynn.
Franco Ventresca complains that the Fossi brothers, protected by Aaron Held, are taking his city territory.
Gunmen fire into Dante and Claire's bedroom, and Dante concludes the order came from inside his own house.
Dante tells Held in the south and Ventresca in the city that he blames the other, setting the two men against each other.
The Fossis garrotte Ventresca in a bar and flee when a policeman walks in, leaving him alive.
In the island capital, Dante watches Held's partners carve up the country and has Held's man Nico Ferra strangled in his hotel room.
Dante's brother Sandro lets slip that he already knew Ferra, and Dante kisses him and disowns him as the island's government collapses around them.
Home again, Dante learns Claire has lost the baby and that Ventresca survived and is talking to federal agents.
At the legislative hearing Ventresca recants his testimony when Dante seats his brother from the old country in the gallery behind him.
Claire tells Dante the miscarriage was an abortion and that she is leaving; he strikes her and keeps the children.
After their mother's funeral Dante has Held shot at an airport, Ventresca persuaded to open his veins, and Sandro shot on the lake.
nonlinear_category_reason: The father's rise and the son's decline alternate on a regular beat, both progressing forward, paired throughout by contrast.
syuzhet_notes: The film braids two threads. Told-order bullets 1, 2, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12 and 18 belong to the father's story and are flashbacks relative to the son's present, which the rest occupy. The final told-order bullet is a further flashback, to a birthday decades before the present, placed after the chronologically latest scene in the film so that the son's isolation is the last image.
fabula_notes: The father's rise between the killing of the extortionist and the founding of the import company is compressed rather than dramatised, as is the long gap between his revenge in the old country and the birthday gathering. Who ordered the bedroom shooting is inferred by the son rather than shown.
